title: Calculated serum osmolarity did not improve grip-strength prediction beyond flexible solute predictors across reused NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested whether a nonlinear calculated-osmolarity feature adds concurrent combined-handgrip information beyond its individual solutes, demographics, body size, creatinine and albumin. Models fitted to NHANES2011–2012 (n=4011) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=4532). Examination-weighted MSE was 133.532 versus 133.743 kg²; delta +0.211, joint source-refit/target PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.580,2.713]. The registered improvement criterion failed. Some weaker comparators yielded small apparent benefits. This negative model-increment audit does not establish physiological absence, equivalence or a causal hydration effect. Both cohorts were previously reused; independent-study validation remains incomplete.
